title: Lamb Biryani

ingredientGroups.title: Lamb Masala
items: 2.2 lbs lamb shoulder, cut into 1-1.5” chunks
2 Tbsp garlic ginger chili paste (2:2:1 ratio, see recipe)
1 cup Barista (fried red onion, see recipe)
1 cup coriander leaves, chopped (2 bunches of cilantro)
½ cup chopped tomatoes (1 large roma)

ingredientGroups.title: Rice
items: 0.5 kg basmati rice (Tilda or Daawat brand)
3 Tbsp garlic ginger chili paste (2:2:1 ratio, see recipe)

ingredientGroups.title: Assembly
items: 1 cup golden raisins (or similar dried fruit)
1 cup Barista (fried red onion, see recipe)
2 Tsp Keora water (kewra, keora, or kewda water)

steps: Prepare the Barista and Garlic-Ginger-Chili paste if necessary.
Soak the saffron strands in ¼ cup medium-hot milk and set aside until assembly.
Combine all the Lamb Masala ingredients and thoroughly mix to coat the chunks of meat. Optionally marinade the mixture for up to 30 minutes.
Cook the Lamb Masala in the Instant Pot using the Meat/Stew mode, high pressure, for 45 minutes.
With 10 minutes remaining on the Instant Pot, rinse the basmati rice in a medium-large bowl until the water runs clear. Cover the rice completely with water and let it soak for 20 minutes.

While the rice is soaking, bring 3 liters of water to a boil in a large pot along with ghee, cinnamon, cumin, green and black cardamom, star anise, cloves, bay leaves, garlic-ginger-chili paste, and salt. Cover and lower the heat to a simmer until you are ready to cook the rice.
Let the Instant Pot naturally release pressure for 10 minutes when the Meat/Stew cycle is complete and then vent the remaining pressure using the quick-release.
Switch the Instant Pot to Saute mode with low heat and simmer the Lamb Masala, stirring occasionally, until the gravy has thickened, approximately 10 more minutes.

Bring the large pot of water back to a rolling boil then strain and add the soaked rice. Cook over high heat until 70% done, approximately 10 minutes. The grains should be tender on the outside with a little bite on the inside, similar to an al dente noodle.
Strain the par cooked rice in a colander.
Add half the lamb masala to the bottom of the large pot.
Add half of the rice, being careful not to compress or break the grains.
Repeat the assembly process again, starting with the lamb.
Finish by drizzling 2 Tbsp ghee, the saffron-milk mixture, and kewra water.
Cook over high heat for 4 minutes and low heat for 10 minutes.
